title: Serre duality and Riemann--Roch for line bundles on nodal curves
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-pc-scheme] [def-kun-projective]. Assume that every singular closed point has completed local ring $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. There is an invertible module $\omega_X$ [def-sc-invertible-module] with functorial $k$-linear isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(F,\omega_X)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1(X,F),k)$$
for every coherent module $F$. Here module cohomology is Zariski cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. For every invertible module $M$, put $g=h^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $N=\omega_X\otimes M^{-1}$, where $M^{-1}=\mathcal Hom(M,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. All the displayed cohomology spaces are finite-dimensional, and
$$h^0(X,N)=h^1(X,M),\quad h^0(X,\omega_X)=g,\quad h^0(X,M)-h^1(X,M)=\deg_X M+1-g.$$
The degree satisfies
$$\deg_XM=\chi(X,M)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=\sum_Z\deg(\nu_Z^*M),$$
where $Z$ runs over the irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components], $\nu_Z:\widetilde Z\to X$ is their normalization [def-sc-normalization], and on each proper smooth normalization the degree is the Euler-characteristic degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. The representing module $\omega_X$ is unique up to the unique isomorphism preserving the displayed duality isomorphisms. Reducedness, pure dimension and connectedness use [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-pure-dimension] [def-weil-connected-scheme]; algebraic closedness is [def-weil-algebraic-closure].

source.place: Tags 0BS2 (lemma-duality-dim-1), 0BS4 (remark-rework-duality-locally-free), 0BS6 (lemma-rr); the nodal specialization is Gorenstein by moduli-curves.tex Tag 0E6R (lemma-gorenstein-dualizing). The component-normalization degree convention follows varieties.tex Tag 0AYU (lemma-degree-birational-pullback), applied to the disjoint normalization; global functions are curves.tex Section genus (proper reduced connected over an algebraically closed field).

proof.text: The structure map $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper because it is projective, hence is of finite type. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so the finite-type Noetherian theorem makes $X$ Noetherian. Finite-type affine $k$-algebras are finitely presented; thus $f$ is locally of finite presentation. It is quasi-compact by finite type and quasi-separated because $X$ is locally Noetherian, hence is of finite presentation. Finally $f$ is flat by field-flatness.

Since $k$ is algebraically closed, its own identity extension can be chosen as its algebraic closure. The only geometric fibre of $f$ in the chosen-algebraic-closure convention is therefore $X$ itself. Its nonemptiness, reducedness, pure dimension one and nodal completed local rings are the hypotheses of the item. Apply the relative nodal dualizing theorem over $\operatorname{Spec}k$: its dualizing module $W$ is invertible and is the fibre's Serre-duality module. Independently, reduced-curve duality supplies the coherent representing module $\omega_X$ with the displayed natural $k$-linear isomorphisms and its uniqueness as a representing pair. As $W$ represents that same functor, this uniqueness identifies $\omega_X$ with $W$. Thus $\omega_X$ is invertible, and the full functorial duality and uniqueness clauses follow.

source.place: Tag 0BS2, lemma-duality-dim-1 (5); moduli-curves.tex Tag 0E6R, lemma-gorenstein-dualizing, specialized to an algebraically closed field.

proof.text: For any invertible $M$, its dual $M^{-1}$ and $N=\omega_X\otimes M^{-1}$ are invertible by tensor-dual closure. On a trivializing open an invertible module is $\mathcal O_X$, so is quasi-coherent of finite type. On the locally Noetherian scheme $X$, the coherent-module criterion makes $M,N,\omega_X$ and $\mathcal O_X$ coherent. Proper coherent-cohomology finiteness applies to each, in every degree. Dimension vanishing applies since $X$ is Noetherian of dimension one: all their $H^q$ for $q>1$ vanish. Thus all displayed spaces are finite-dimensional and $\chi(X,L)=h^0(X,L)-h^1(X,L)$ for each of these line modules $L$.

source.place: Tag 02O6, lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite; Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian; cohomology.tex Tag 02UZ, proposition-vanishing-Noetherian.

proof.text: There is a canonical $k$-linear bijection $H^0(X,\omega_X\otimes M^{-1})\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,\omega_X)$: on a trivializing open with generator $e$ and dual generator $e^\vee$, send $w\otimes e^\vee$ to the map $ae\mapsto aw$. The inverse sends $\phi$ to $\phi(e)\otimes e^\vee$. Replacing $e$ by $ue$ multiplies $\phi(e)$ by $u$ and $e^\vee$ by $u^{-1}$, so both constructions agree on overlaps and glue. Compose with the duality isomorphism of step 2 at $F=M$. Taking dimensions gives $h^0(X,N)=h^1(X,M)$: for a finite basis of a vector space its coordinate functionals are a basis of its dual, so the two dimensions agree. Taking $M=\mathcal O_X$ gives $h^0(X,\omega_X)=h^1(X,\mathcal O_X)=g$.

source.place: Tag 0BS4, remark-rework-duality-locally-free; the rank-one Hom identification is written out.

proof.text: The global-functions theorem applies to $X$: it is nonempty, proper, connected, reduced and one-dimensional over the algebraically closed field $k$. Hence $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, and step 3 gives $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=1-g$. By the Euler-characteristic definition of degree, $\deg_X M=\chi(X,M)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Substitute the preceding equality and $\chi(X,M)=h^0(X,M)-h^1(X,M)$ to obtain $h^0(X,M)-h^1(X,M)=\deg_X M+1-g$. This is an integer rearrangement; no smoothness of $X$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0BUG, lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections (2),(3), and degree Definition 0AYR; curves.tex Tag 0BS6, lemma-rr, rank-one numerical specialization.

proof.text: Apply the weighted-component degree formula to $X$ and $M$. It gives finitely many reduced integral proper one-dimensional components $Z$ and $\deg_XM=\sum_Z m_Z\deg_Z(M|_Z)$. At a component-generic point $\eta$, reduced-curve duality explicitly asserts that $\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ is a field. As a module over itself a field has only the submodules $0$ and itself, so has length one: $m_Z=1$. Therefore $\deg_XM=\sum_Z\deg_Z(M|_Z)$.

source.place: Tag 0AYW, lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components; reducedness makes every generic multiplicity one.

proof.text: The reduced-curve normalization theorem gives that each $\widetilde Z$ is a smooth proper connected curve. Fix a component $Z$; by step 6 it is an integral scheme proper over $k$ of dimension one, hence separated and of finite type, i.e. a proper curve. Normalization properties give that $\widetilde Z\to Z$ is finite, surjective and birational, that $\widetilde Z$ is proper over $k$ and that $\dim\widetilde Z=1$. By the definition of the normalization, over a nonempty affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Z$ the scheme $\widetilde Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with $A'$ the integral closure of the domain $A$ in $K=k(Z)$; so $A'$ is a domain with fraction field $K$, and its generic point is the only point over the generic point of $Z$. All these affine pieces therefore share one generic point, so $\widetilde Z$ is integral with $k(\widetilde Z)=K$, and is a proper curve. The map $\widetilde Z\to Z$ is dominant, and the extension $k(Z)\to k(\widetilde Z)$ is the identity of $K$, so it is finite of degree $d=1$. The proper-curve pullback-degree theorem applied to this morphism and the line bundle $M|_Z$ gives $\deg_{\widetilde Z}(\nu_Z^*M)=1\cdot\deg_Z(M|_Z)$. Here pulling back the restriction along $\widetilde Z\to Z$ is pulling back along the composite $\nu_Z:\widetilde Z\to X$, by the functorial pullback isomorphism. Substitute this equality into the sum of step 6. It gives precisely the asserted normalization-component formula with the same Euler-characteristic degree on each smooth normalization.
